# LL-G Lessons Learned & Gotchas

> Machine-readable knowledge base of coding gotchas. Before scripting, load this file, then load the llms.txt for each technology you are about to use. Load only HIGH-severity entries unless a specific topic is relevant.

## Severity Legend

HIGH = silent wrong output or hard-to-debug errors -- always load these
MEDIUM = obvious failures (build errors, test failures) -- load when relevant
LOW = style/convention, caught by linter -- skip unless explicitly asked

> Keep each line below to one clause naming the technology and its scope. The specific
> gotchas belong on the shelf, not here -- this file is a router that every session loads.

### Bash
- [Bash index](kb/bash/llms.txt): bash shell scripting and pattern-matching gotchas; gh api printing the HTTP error body on STDOUT so the idiomatic `x=$(gh api ... --jq .field 2>/dev/null || true)` captures 404 JSON instead of an empty string (--jq does not filter an error body), which a forgiving endpoint can then swallow -- the contents API ignores a bogus sha when creating a file; and a base64 payload passed as an argv element outgrowing the ~32 KB Windows/msys command-line limit as the target file grows, failing with exit 126 that names the interpreter rather than the payload (21 entries)
